title: ZnO-integrated konjac glucomannan/Bletilla striata hydrogel with antibacterial, anti-inflammatory, and pro-angiogenic properties for accelerated infected wound healing.
abstract: Accelerating the healing of infected wounds remains a significant clinical challenge due to the complex interplay between persistent infection and impaired cellular signaling. Herein, we developed a bio-inspired, multifunctional hydrogel (KGMBSP@ZnO) by synergistically crosslinking konjac glucomannan (KGM) and Bletilla striata polysaccharide (BSP) to create a pro-regenerative microenvironment. Beyond its robust mechanical toughness and self-healing properties, this study uncovers the hydrogel's dual-functional role in infection eradication and bio-instructed tissue remodeling. Mechanistically, KGMBSP@ZnO does not merely act as an antibacterial barrier; it actively directs wound repair by orchestrating the macrophage-to-myofibroblast transition (MMT)-a critical yet under-explored pathway in material-mediated regeneration. In vitro analysis reveals that the hydrogel's bioactive matrix triggers endothelial proliferation and migration through the integrated activation of PI3K/Akt, MAPK/ERK, and Rho GTPase pathways. In a murine infected wound model, the hydrogel effectively suppressed chronic inflammation by modulating the TNF-α/NF-κB and IL-10 signaling axes while significantly promoting functional angiogenesis and organized collagen deposition. Our findings demonstrate that the KGMBSP@ZnO hydrogel provides a promising "immunomodulatory-to-regenerative" strategy, shifting the paradigm from passive wound dressing to an active therapeutic platform that modulates macrophage plasticity to achieve rapid, high-quality tissue regeneration.
